bicycle.named_subject: A bicycle front wheel with spokes, seen close up, with a few straight lines of the bicycle frame at its upper right
bicycle.action: The wheel stays in roughly the same place while its spokes change arrangement from frame to frame, and in the second half a second frame line appears and the wheel outline opens a gap at the lower right.
bicycle.identity_gap: The wheel matches the doodle's segmented polygon rim and star of spokes, but only one wheel and two frame lines of the doodle are shown, so the seat, handlebar and second wheel are missing.
bicycle.notes: The film shows a front wheel rolling steadily while a rider pedals, and the animation keeps the wheel position but redraws the spokes at unrelated angles each frame instead of turning them in one direction, with sudden extra lines appearing at frames 9 to 12. The change that would help most is to rotate a single fixed spoke set by a consistent small angle per frame so the wheel visibly turns like the film's wheel.
bicycle._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

butterfly.named_subject: a butterfly with two lobed wings, a long segmented body, a round head and antennae
butterfly.action: The butterfly sits on a fingertip as the hand moves left and up, and its wings narrow and tilt more upright toward the end of the shot.
butterfly.identity_gap: The animated butterfly keeps the doodle's lobed wing outlines, the ladder-marked body line that extends past the wings, the small circle head and the two antennae, only made smaller and narrower.
butterfly.notes: Most of the leftward travel happens in one step between frames 1 and 2, while in the film the hand drifts over frames 1 to 4, and the wings narrow suddenly at frame 13. Spreading the frame 1 to 2 move across frames 1 to 4 would help most.
butterfly._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

cat.named_subject: a cat's face (head with two pointed ears, two eyes and whiskers)
cat.action: The cat head holds nearly still with a slight tilt and sway for most of the shot, then shrinks and shifts to the right in the last four frames.
cat.identity_gap: The head outline, ears, top notch and hexagonal eyes match the doodle, but the left whiskers are regrouped into a downward-angled fan instead of the doodle's three roughly horizontal strokes, and the whole head is tilted.
cat.notes: Frames 1-12 match the film's upward-looking, mostly still head, but in the film the cat turns its head to a right-facing profile at frame 13, while the drawing only jumps smaller and to the right without turning. The change that would help most is to animate the head turn across frames 12-14 (eyes and ears shifting toward the right side, the face narrowing) instead of a sudden scale and position jump.
cat._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

cow.named_subject: a cow's head, seen close up, with a large rounded muzzle, ears, short horns and a spotted body behind it
cow.action: The cow's head tilts slightly in the first frames and then settles upright facing the viewer, holding nearly still with a small smile while a body spot shifts near the end.
cow.identity_gap: The head uses the doodle's oval ear, tick-mark eyes, wide rounded muzzle with a small curved mouth and outlined spots, but the oval left ear is replaced by two loose strokes from frame 6 onward, which the doodle never has.
cow.notes: The film shows the cow turning from a three-quarter view to face the camera and then opening its mouth repeatedly; the animation gets the early tilt and the frontal hold but the mouth never opens, the drawing shifts down and redraws between frames 4 and 6, and a spot jumps at frame 15. The one change that would help most is animating the mouth opening and closing on the muzzle in frames 4-16 to match the film's chewing or mooing while keeping the oval ear constant.
cow._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

dog.named_subject: a four-legged animal with a long neck and a pointed snout, most likely a dog
dog.action: The animal stands facing left with its head raised, then turns to face right, lowers its head, and ends with its head down near the bowl.
dog.identity_gap: The animated figure keeps the doodle's diamond-shaped head with the eye, long neck, boxy rear and loop legs, but in later frames the rear box and legs are drawn twice so the body looks duplicated.
dog.notes: The film shows the dog looking up at the person, turning, walking toward the camera and then moving to the bowl; the animation gets the head-up start and head-down end but turns from left to right in a single frame (5 to 6) and changes body length and head height abruptly at frames 8, 10 and 13, and it never shows the walk toward the camera. The change that would help most is adding in-between frames for the turn so the body rotates over several frames instead of flipping at once.
dog._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

duck.named_subject: a duck or goose standing in side view, facing left, with small webbed feet
duck.action: The bird stays in place in profile and its outline wobbles and shifts slightly, while the beak and head shape change size in a few frames; it never turns to face the viewer.

Every fourth frame (4, 8, 12, 16) the head and beak redraw larger with doubled beak lines, which reads as a pop; the change that would help most is to animate the head turning toward the viewer in frames 3-4 as in the film, with the head drawn consistently between keys.
duck._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

fan.named_subject: an electric desk fan seen from the front: a rounded housing with three curved blades around a scribbled hub, standing on a short hatched base
fan.action: The three curved blades turn around the central hub while the round housing and the base stay still.
fan.identity_gap: The animated fan keeps the doodle's lopsided outline, small tick at the top, dense scribbled hub, three curved blade lines and hatched base, so it reads as the same drawing.
fan.notes: The film shows a fan spinning fast, and the drawing does turn its blades, but the blade positions change by uneven amounts between frames, so the rotation has no steady direction or speed, and in frames 7, 8 and 9 a blade runs past the housing outline down into the base. The one change that would help most is to rotate the blades by an equal angle in one direction each frame and clip them to the housing outline.
fan._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

flying-saucer.named_subject: a flying saucer (UFO) with a domed top and small windows, turned on its side

flying-saucer._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

giraffe.named_subject: a giraffe head and upper neck in close-up, with two ossicones on top, an ear on the left, an eye mark and a long snout

giraffe.identity_gap: The head, ossicones, ear, eye arrow and jaw construction match the doodle closely, but the shot crops off most of the doodle's long neck and its inner neck strokes.
giraffe.notes: The film shows the giraffe chewing with its mouth opening and closing and a second ear coming into view, while the animation only resizes the snout outline in a few steps (frame 5 shrinks it, frame 9 adds split neck lines, frame 13 flattens the jaw). giraffe._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

helicopter.named_subject: a helicopter (side view, with main rotor, cockpit, skid struts, landing skid and tail boom)

helicopter.notes: Frames 1-6 and 9-16 move smoothly, but between frames 6 and 8 the body tilts and the tail and skid appear in about two steps while the film tilts more gradually, and rotor blades in frames 2, 4 and 6 are drawn as doubled lines; a grey scenery shape also sits on top of the body from frame 8 on. helicopter._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

horse.named_subject: a horse's head and neck in profile, with a zigzag mane, seen beside a fence

horse.identity_gap: The construction matches the doodle (zigzag mane, pointed ears, scribbled dot eye, open jaw curve, two neck lines), but one ear is drawn as a sideways pointed shape sticking out of the neck line rather than upright as in the doodle.

horse._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

hurricane.named_subject: a flat, pointed, boat-like scribble (a canoe or low boat shape made of overlapping strokes), drawn twice, one copy stacked above the other
hurricane.action: The stacked pair of boat shapes slides steadily from left to right across a grey outline of a house roof, while further copies of the pair slide in at the right edge (frames 1-5) and then at the left edge (frames 9-16).
hurricane.identity_gap: Each copy uses the same long overlapping strokes and pointed right end as c.png, but the drawing appears two to four times per frame instead of once.

hurricane._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

monkey.named_subject: a monkey (head with round ears, muzzle, and a curled tail, seated)
monkey.action: The monkey slides left and slightly down while its face features shift toward the left edge of the head, holds that position, then returns to a front-facing pose in the last two frames.
monkey.identity_gap: The drawing keeps the doodle's head outline, spiral eye, muzzle loop, ear shapes and spiral tail, but in frames 5-14 the left ear is cut off by the top of the frame and the left eye is squeezed into overlapping lines.
monkey.notes: The film shows the head turning to screen-left and tilting down so the face points at the ground, but the animation mostly translates the whole drawing and slides the face features sideways, with no downward tilt of the head and a sudden snap back between frames 14 and 15. monkey._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

mosquito.named_subject: a mosquito (insect with an upright wing, thin legs, round head and a long curved proboscis) standing on a slope
mosquito.action: The mosquito stays in place on a sloped line and its body and wing bob slightly up and down, while the slope and hair marks shift a little between frames.
mosquito.identity_gap: The animated character is the c.png drawing mirrored to face left, with the same tall triangular wing, oval head, long curved proboscis and stick legs, only drawn smaller.
mosquito.notes: The film shows a mosquito on hairy skin feeding with its proboscis pressed into the skin, but in the animation the skin-edge line runs through the mosquito's body and the proboscis curls into empty air, and at frame 10 the whole hair and ground layer jumps left. The change that would help most is to put the mosquito on the skin surface so the proboscis touches it, and to keep the scenery from jumping at frame 10.
mosquito._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

pig.named_subject: a pig seen from the side, with a spiral snout, two pointed ears, a round body and short stick legs
pig.action: The pig stands still in profile for six frames, then shrinks and slides right, then grows larger and tilts its body so the head drops lower and to the left while the legs spread.
pig.identity_gap: The drawing keeps the doodle's spiral snout, zigzag ears, open body outline and split leg strokes, but in frames 11-16 the body is rotated and swollen so the outline proportions drift from the doodle.
pig.notes: The film shows the pig standing, then turning its head toward the camera and walking forward so it grows larger in frame, but the animation first shrinks the pig in frames 8-9 and then rotates the whole flat side-view drawing instead of turning the head, and the size changes at frames 8, 9 and 11 read as pops. The one change that would help most is to remove the shrink in frames 7-9 and make the growth a steady increase across frames 7-16 so the pig scales up continuously as it approaches the camera.
pig._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

rabbit.action: The rabbit comes out from behind a door edge, turns to face right and sits hunched by the wall with its ears lowering back, then runs off to the right out of frame.
rabbit.identity_gap: The animated rabbit uses the same open single-line outline, two long pointed ears, spike front leg and bumped rump as the doodle, mirrored to face right, though the head in frames 1-2 is drawn tall and narrow and loses the doodle's rounded snout.
rabbit.notes: The poses track the film closely through the sit and the exit, but the body outline appears suddenly at frame 3, the ears swap positions abruptly at frames 7 and 13, the front leg draws as a small closed loop at frame 12, and the ear detaches from the head at frame 15. The change that would help most is smoothing the ear transitions between the upright, laid-back and running poses so the ears do not jump between frames.
rabbit._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

raccoon.named_subject: a raccoon (round smiling face with ears, oval body, four stick legs, striped ringed tail)
raccoon.action: The raccoon stands side-on facing left at the edge of tall grass and drifts slightly left while its head tips downward and then rotates to a more upright, larger oval, with the legs staying almost fixed.
raccoon.identity_gap: The animated figure uses the same angular head with ear, dot eyes and smile, oval body, four stick legs with a hooked front foot, and banded tail as c.png, with only the head proportions changing in later frames.
raccoon.notes: The figure holds one pose for most of the shot while the film raccoon lowers its head to forage and turns its body; at frame 9 the scenery shifts abruptly and at frame 13 the head is redrawn larger and more upright. The change that would help most is to drive the head drop and body turn from the film, including leg steps, instead of keeping the legs fixed and only resizing the head.
raccoon._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

rain.named_subject: rain: many short dark vertical streaks falling over a house, a tree and a zigzag fence
rain.action: Short rain streaks fill the frame and are redrawn in new positions each frame as if falling, at roughly constant density, while the grey house, tree and fence stay in place with slight line wobble.
rain.identity_gap: The streaks match the doodle's short, slightly slanted single strokes, including the occasional kinked stroke, but the animation uses far more of them at more uniform lengths than the doodle.
rain.notes: The rain falls at a steady density throughout, while the film's rain grows heavier and darker over the shot and the water on the bridge surface splashes more; the grey scenery (house, tree, zigzag fence) also does not match the film's bridge with converging railings. The one change that would help most is to increase the rain density and streak length from frame 1 to frame 16 to match the film's build-up, and add splash marks at the bottom.
rain._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

roller-coaster.named_subject: a roller coaster lift hill: a double-rail track with cross-tie hatch marks rising to a peak, with two support lines sloping down to the right
roller-coaster.action: The track rotates from a moderate slope to a near-vertical climb and narrows over frames 1-9, then holds nearly still through frame 16.
roller-coaster.identity_gap: The animated track has the doodle's double rail, short slanted hatch ties and two descending lines, but it is much steeper and narrower than the doodle's shallow bent climb for most of the shot.
roller-coaster.notes: The track's steepening matches the film's camera reframing, but the scenery pops in frame 6 (both clouds vanish, then return in frame 7) and nothing shows the coaster car climbing the hill, which is the main motion in the film. The one change that would help most is adding the car moving up the track, following the film.
roller-coaster._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

sailboat.named_subject: a sailboat with one triangular sail, a mast and a long hull, on water with two small grey boats in the distance

sailboat._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

see-saw.named_subject: a seesaw: a long plank resting on a triangular pivot, tilted down to the right

see-saw.identity_gap: The animated plank is a little flatter and shorter than in the doodle, but the outline, the stray tick at the top-left corner, the doubled pivot strokes and the small dot all match c.png.
see-saw.notes: The film's near seesaw also holds a steady downward tilt to the right while a woman lifts a child onto it, so the near-static drawing matches the board but shows nothing of the activity in the shot. The change that would help most is to have the plank rock or dip visibly when the child is placed on it around frames 9-14, so the drawing shows the event in the film.
see-saw._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

sheep._protocol: 16 frames, motion_score 1-5, same packet for Giraffe Walks Past

windmill.named_subject: a windmill: a tall box-shaped tower with a domed top and several long blades joined at a central hub

__gwp__.named_subject: a giraffe, drawn as a straight-line stick figure with a long neck, a small wedge-shaped head with two horns, a box body and four legs
__gwp__.action: The giraffe walks from the left side of the frame toward the right, past a bare tree, with two young giraffes in the background, as in the film.
__gwp__.identity_gap: The doodle is a large close-up giraffe head and neck with a rounded muzzle, mouth line, eye, ear and knobbed horns, while the animation is a small full-body stick giraffe whose head is a plain triangle wedge with none of those features.
__gwp__.notes: The path, direction and pacing follow the film, but the legs pop into unrelated poses in frames 2 (a rearing, bent-leg pose) and 5 (legs splayed apart), several frames show doubled front-leg lines, and in frames 15 and 16 the body shortens and the legs bunch together.
